a.text: Isabelle Montague, loyal Victorian Knight of the Tower once said—

spans.text: Isabelle Montague, loyal Victorian Knight of the Tower once said—

a.text: 'History is like a granary.'

spans.text: 'History is like a granary.'

a.text: It stands in silence amidst the bustling estate, an unremarkable sight with a somewhat unpleasant scent of mold. Only ever thought of when stowing something away.

spans.text: It stands in silence amidst the bustling estate, an unremarkable sight with a somewhat unpleasant scent of mold. Only ever thought of when stowing something away.

a.text: Containment. Silently containing things is its sole purpose.

spans.text: Containment. Silently containing things is its sole purpose.

a.text: As for people, they are like stalks of wheat growing out in the fields, braving the elements so they might sprout those precious, precious ears.

spans.text: As for people, they are like stalks of wheat growing out in the fields, braving the elements so they might sprout those precious, precious ears.

a.text: All you have experienced will become shining, golden grain, stored within the granary called history.

spans.text: All you have experienced will become shining, golden grain, stored within the granary called history.

a.text: It's more apt to say that history is a showroom of human lives.

spans.text: It's more apt to say that history is a showroom of human lives.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Shining and golden? Yeah, I'd say that was a shining, golden life...

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: Vina, the sword is yours.

steps.name: Impassioned Voice
steps.text: It is your destiny.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Father, is this...?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina! The hell're you doing?!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Stop swinging already! You've nearly beaten him dead!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: *huff*... *huff*...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Vina! It's time!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Vina, who do you wish to be when you leave this palace?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I choose—

a.text: Perhaps this is how history runs its course. Those caught up in its flow won't accept things as they are, they will resist it with all their might.

spans.text: Perhaps this is how history runs its course. Those caught up in its flow won't accept things as they are, they will resist it with all their might.

a.text: But reality always comes crashing down, slamming you into the ground over and over.

spans.text: But reality always comes crashing down, slamming you into the ground over and over.

a.text: You've got no choice but to get back up and figure a way to stand firm. You know the fight'll never end, and you've got to make ready for the next fist in your face.

spans.text: You've got no choice but to get back up and figure a way to stand firm. You know the fight'll never end, and you've got to make ready for the next fist in your face.

a.text: Until you've circled round and round to find yourself back where you started, albeit by some different path—

spans.text: Until you've circled round and round to find yourself back where you started, albeit by some different path—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Wait, now that I think about it, Dagda might've said 'millstone'.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: 'History is like a millstone'?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I forgot what metaphor she used exactly, just that it's got to do with a mill or a windmill or something. The sort of thing that'll get people thinking of the sunset.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Ah, forget it. I never much fancied the way she talks all erudite like.

a.text: When all's done, I'm here to record this... heart-pounding moment in history.

spans.text: When all's done, I'm here to record this... heart-pounding moment in history.

a.text: As a witness to this particular point, as one who personally experienced some of these events, I felt the need to share the tale with those who come after.

spans.text: As a witness to this particular point, as one who personally experienced some of these events, I felt the need to share the tale with those who come after.

a.text: It's worth remembering, considering the many bitter lessons learned. It must not be forgotten, with too many painful sacrifices made.

spans.text: It's worth remembering, considering the many bitter lessons learned. It must not be forgotten, with too many painful sacrifices made.

a.text: Safe to say, the story's so twisty and turny that if you weren't there to see for yourself, you'd never guess where it ended up—

spans.text: Safe to say, the story's so twisty and turny that if you weren't there to see for yourself, you'd never guess where it ended up—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Aha! I remember now! It was a ship!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: 'History is like a sailing ship adrift, and every age sees its share of experienced helmsmen who think to change its course...'

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: 'But in the end, none will truly ever know where the sunset and the river will take them—'

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Bah, sod it, I don't need to copy the feel of those historical novels I read. It's my book. Why should I write it like how Vina's governess talks?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Lemme have a think on how I'd tell the story my way...

a.text: This here's a tale of how a hoodlum became a hero. It's all about courage, friendship, conviction, and power.

spans.text: This here's a tale of how a hoodlum became a hero. It's all about courage, friendship, conviction, and power.

a.text: The heir to the King leaves the palace, and when she returns home, she's already fit to be called hero, standing alongside her merry band of mates.

spans.text: The heir to the King leaves the palace, and when she returns home, she's already fit to be called hero, standing alongside her merry band of mates.

a.text: This epic begins the summer of the year we left, in the factories of Londinium's Norport Borough.

spans.text: This epic begins the summer of the year we left, in the factories of Londinium's Norport Borough.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: ...They were the happiest days of my life.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Muncaster.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Mm-hmm.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: ...Bristol.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Got any more?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Sheffi... Di... No, Glou—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Baird! Gimme a hint already! Vina? You really gonna watch me embarrass myself like this?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Hey, it's your bet. I can't say anything.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Baird's right, wouldn't be fair otherwise.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Don't give up now, Indra. Victoria's got at least sixty or so nomadic cities. If you can think of one more, you're a sixth of the way there.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: My whole life I've never left Londinium. It's my home. Why the hell would I remember what some cities miles away are called?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You must be real fond of cleaning up the alleys back home, then.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Dammit, I shouldn't be acting like a smartarse!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Oh, Hannah, do you still recall the time we went to the video shop? After we were done duffing the Lane Brothers up?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I think I do? Didn't the film have a manor with white walls and a green lawn... Was it some kinda romance? It just went on and on.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Then do you remember what the leading lady loved eating the most at the nobles' banquets—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: 'Sidmouth butter and vanilla roast fowlbeast'!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Yeah! Sidmouth! That's ten!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: *sigh*... Vina.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You really are the best when it comes to leading, Vina! I'll follow you my entire life, I will!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No need to get all sappy on me now.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Alright, Morgan, you lost. Here's your drink.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You know Vina helped her out, Baird... Ah, whatevs, drink's a drink.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Morgan! It's your turn to pick up the protection money from the factories on Old Farleigh Road.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Don't forget to help clean up the alleyways behind Old Hank's sandwich shop.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It's times like these that Glasgow feels spread a bit thin.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Hah, one day, I'm gonna make all of Londinium into Glasgow Gang turf, and all those fees will come straight to us! Alongside the best sandwiches in the city!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: If you took all of Victoria under your wing, who'd you even protect them from? The Gaulish?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Maybe those snotty nobles? Who knows, some tosser's bound to show his face sooner or later.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Norport can't make do without us, and neither can Londinium. There'll come a day when Glasgow's the heroes of the whole city, just you wait.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Not wrong, I'd say.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Indeed. Here's to the Glasgow Gang, the most important gang in town.

steps.name: Glasgow Gang
steps.text: To the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Cheerful Noble
steps.text: Did you enjoy the play?

steps.name: Cheerful Noble
steps.text: A Victorian duke's daughter falls in 'love' with a handsome Sarkaz youth.

steps.name: Cheerful Noble
steps.text: In order to eliminate this formidable rival, her would-be suitors conjure all sorts of dreadful devilish plots.

steps.name: Cheerful Noble
steps.text: Who would have thought the playwright who penned The Lady of Windsor could produce such a provocative work, albeit only after a hefty writer's fee.

spans.text: Who would have thought the playwright who penned
The Lady of Windsor
could produce such a provocative work, albeit only after a hefty writer's fee.

steps.name: Cheerful Noble
steps.text: What do you think, Lady Allerdale?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I can't say I'm too fond of the ending of Cemeteries of Londinium, Earl Morrill.

spans.text: I can't say I'm too fond of the ending of
Cemeteries of Londinium
, Earl Morrill.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Under the heavy hand of persecution, the Duke's daughter and the Sarkaz lad elope, united in death as they are buried together in a public cemetery. A conclusion that's far too... formulaic.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: I never expected a young lady such as yourself to have the tastes of a haranguing critic.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Is it not enough to bring tears to your eyes?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: To whose eyes? Duke Cavendish's, or the Sarkaz Regent's?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Tears will only serve to blind us, my Lord, and are often an accomplice to popular works harboring ill intent.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: A shame, truly. Here I was, thinking you would have some empathy for the leading lady, what with her bound to a fate beyond her control.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Ah, I am so dreadfully sorry! Pray forgive my inadvertent offense. You must know that my family was once on good terms with the Cumberlands...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I don't really mind.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It's common knowledge that Her Grace the Duke of Caster aided me at my lowest. I have only gratitude for her. I see no shame in my circumstances either.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Then since you're taking part in today's festivities, may I takes your words as Her Grace's own thoughts?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: You may consider them a friendly reminder.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Londiniers should be wary of those mercenaries from Kazdel, heaven forbid some ridiculous story to sow the seeds of pity and sympathy in their unwitting minds.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Kazdel is far, far away, and they simply don't understand these Sarkaz in the slightest. Do not allow tears to blind their judgment, my Lord.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Your words would throttle a talented playwright.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Bringing the citizenry to tears would hardly be a difficult thing for a duke, I say.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Is this also Her Grace's opinion on the matter?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No matter what you might think of this playwright, I do believe 'The Lady of Windsor' is a rare work of art. I whole-heartedly invite you—and perhaps Duke Cavendish—to give it a thorough read-through.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: 'Fins have not the limbs to drag themselves out of the swamp. Man has not the eye to see beyond time.'

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: If Duke Cavendish can understand these words and take them to heart, while keeping a wary eye on this matter, he can avoid becoming the next Duke Windsor.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No offense meant, of course.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Oho, I must say I quite enjoy your incisive view on this topic, Lady Allerdale.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: The eye to see beyond time... A rare thing indeed. In comparison, ambition beyond one's means is as cheap as chips, wouldn't you say?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I can't say I disagree.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Despite the many years past, there are still those who have not forgotten that Victoria once had a king.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: And there are those who carry the former heir to the throne in mind, alongside that sword of royal authority.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Duke Caster's actions are hardly inscrutable. Whenever she dispenses advice to the other dukes, do not forget that there are eyes upon her in turn.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I will inform Her Grace, my Lord.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It's getting late. I fear I must be heading off.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Not staying for dinner, Lady Cumberland?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I have an appointment with my tailor to prepare some winter clothes. I'm sure you're aware that summer in Londinium lasts but a few fleeting days—

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: But winter? Winter never comes late.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Then I shan't keep you any longer, my Lady.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: I shall send a ticket for opening night to you beforehand. If Her Grace would like to watch, Duke Cavendish would happily sponsor the troupe to tour the Caster demesne.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I pray that Her Grace will not be blinded by her own tears.
A most suffocating banquet, was it not?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: And who might you be?
You may call me Clovisia. Based on that distinctive white hair of yours, you must be Lady Allerdale Cumberland.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Madam Ailshie of your estate has ordered some outfits for the upcoming season from our shop, but I'm afraid we haven't finalized the details of yours quite yet.

spans.text: Madam Ailshie of your estate
has
ordered some outfits for the upcoming season from our shop, but I'm afraid we haven't finalized the details of yours quite yet.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Sorry, I couldn't help but overhear your conversation with Earl Morris. It seems your reputation as a critic of the arts is well-earned.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: You flatter me. I presume you too are concerned about the present situation in Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Hardly, hardly. It's just rather difficult to not listen in as the clientèle discuss the recent changes when you work at a tailor's.

spans.text: Hardly, hardly. It's just rather difficult to
not
listen in as the clientèle discuss the recent changes when you work at a tailor's.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: *sigh* It's getting dark. I should head home. Once you've settled on a design, please have Madam Ailshie contact me at your convenience.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Ah, right, speaking of Madam Ailshie, she asked me to pass you the Londinium Daily.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Farewell.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Might as well see if there's anything else newsworthy today, I suppose.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: A vicious brawl in Norport Borough?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Is that...?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Feckin' 'ell! That's bloody ridiculous is what it is!

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: It's the third time this month. Been accident after accident here in the factory ever since that scoundrel took over the union.

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: Watch close enough and you start to notice how whenever some brave soul puts out a complaint about the union, he ends up dead in some freak accident a few days later.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Let's go then already! Take me to 'im. I'm gonna see just how brass this bastard's balls are!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Calm down! The union handles union business, the street handles street business. That's the rule.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Giving every bastard  I see a right thrashing's my rule!

spans.text: Giving every bastard  I see a right thrashing's
my
rule!

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: I know! Of course I know... But we've got no other choice.

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: The union's keeping it all hush-hush inside the factory. Not even the coppers can investigate.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: This new foreman... Johnny, right? Who's behind him?

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: I remember hearing he's got some big name backing him. A relative of Duke Davendich, apparently...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Do you mean Duke Cavendish?

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: Yeah! That's the one!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Is he trying to get anything out of you lot?

steps.name: Wronged Worker
steps.text: Hasn't been asking for money or any of the sort... but ever since he became foreman, lots of the important jobs are getting taken up by workers from outside.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I see. You head on back. We need to talk this over a bit.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: What're we waiting around for, Morgan?! Are we gonna let these bastards do as they like?!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It's not that simple.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You heard the man. This isn't your average union tosser. He's got the backing of a duke. Why's he going out of his way to play tyrant in some little factory, though?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Who cares why?! Since when did we need a reason to take out buggers like him?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I know Londinium's rather restless these days. The dukes've been playing their games around the clock. Don't tell me you haven't noticed all these fresh faces on the street lately?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Time to come up with a plan, Vina. We're all ears.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Since we've taken their protection money, it's up to us to do the legwork.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Let's go have a chat with this bastard of a foreman. Doesn't matter if he's got a duke behind him.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: That's more like it!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Alright, if you say so, Vina...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: But just to be safe, we should scope out the factory a bit, get some info. You're with me, Baird.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Hey! Why didn't you ask me?!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What's wrong? You've been looking rather glum lately.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: It's nothing. I was just thinking... I might be enjoying myself a little too much.

spans.text: It's nothing. I was just thinking... I might be enjoying myself a little
too
much.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What, not too happy here?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: You have a duty, Siege.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I've told you before, Dagda.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I've found a life for myself now, so why—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Is this life of yours helping your neighbors seek the justice of the streets, then heading to the noble manors to lob a few bricks?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: There's no escaping some things.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You promised me you wouldn't talk about this in the gym.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Then I'll stay by your side, waiting for the day you have your answer.

a.text: Life is long, but the pivotal moments that change you? They're over in an instant.

spans.text: Life is long, but the pivotal moments that change you? They're over in an instant.

a.text: I recall that one afternoon, before the chaos of the storm struck us, when we could still enjoy those peaceful hours.

spans.text: I recall that one afternoon, before the chaos of the storm struck us, when we could still enjoy those peaceful hours.

a.text: Indra didn't speak to me the whole day on account of my hesitation. Baird had to step in and smooth things over between us, and by nightfall we were all happy as could be, buying hot dogs and beer.

spans.text: Indra didn't speak to me the whole day on account of my hesitation. Baird had to step in and smooth things over between us, and by nightfall we were all happy as could be, buying hot dogs and beer.

a.text: But I couldn't shake off the feeling that the Glasgow Gang was about to enter the craziest chapter of this story yet.

spans.text: But I couldn't shake off the feeling that the Glasgow Gang was about to enter the craziest chapter of this story yet.

a.text: It wasn't until those wild dreams of ours came to an end that I realized the most pressing issue...

spans.text: It wasn't until those wild dreams of ours came to an end that I realized the most pressing issue...

a.text: The main character of this tale wasn't the Glasgow Gang. It was Vina. Just Vina, all along.

spans.text: The main character of this tale wasn't the Glasgow Gang. It was Vina. Just Vina, all along.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: What's the matter, Ailshie?

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: Did you not instruct us to keep a close eye on Her Royal Highness Alexandrina's whereabouts?

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: The chief of the Royal Police has just looked over the case file of that ghastly brawl in Norport.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: It involved a video shop known as McClaren's Place and a street gang going by the name of Glasgow.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: Here is the original copy of the file.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: It's rather vague, merely a record of the involved parties, but I thought you ought to know.
Upon a fuzzy black-and-white photograph, a woman sucking on a lollipop stares indignantly at the camera.
'Person of Interest: Siege (self-identified)'

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: Miss Allerdale, if you are near-certain she is Her Royal Highness... Why not seek her out immediately?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: And what then? I bring her back to Cumberland Manor? Or send her off to Caster?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Whether or not she is Alexandrina no longer matters. The dukes are watching her closely. She can escape them no longer.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: It sounds to me like she would be swallowed by the city itself.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Hah. We'll be swallowed too, Ailshie.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm willing to bet we're not the only ones with an interest in her. This matter has long since grown out of my control.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: Considering Duke Caster's orders, should you not find her and bring her to Her Grace?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I need some time to think, Ailshie.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I saw her once before. I saw...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Her Royal Highness.

steps.name: Ailshie
steps.text: But no matter how you put it, it was all such a long time ago. Things being what they are, is an unknown heir truly so important?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It's merely an inkling... From the very first time I saw her, so many years ago, I always believed she would change things.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Let's go. There's a few workers I need to pop in on. I would also like to know how Her Highness has been doing these past few years.

steps.name: Cruel Foreman
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Cruel Foreman
steps.text: Grk—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The coast is clear.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I've handled this side too.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: This is it. The place Charlie told us about.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We heard some chatter. Lately, the union's been keeping a whole bunch of goods inside this old factory, like they were a smuggling ring.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Johnny seized control of the union not just to skim some funds, but to do this sort of business.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: What's inside those containers?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Just open 'em up and we'll find out—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Hannah! Slow—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Are those...?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...Originium weapons.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: They're not standard Victorian issue. No idea of their actual provenance though.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Duke Cavendish's man sneakily taking over a factory, all so he can move weapons from God-knows-where into Londinium? What's he playing at here?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The dukes quietly stockpiling weapons within the city can only mean one thing.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: And now we've left our fingerprints all over the place...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: What do we do now, Vina? Looks to me like it's something way bigger than we can handle.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: We can't handle it ourselves, but we can tell others.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Got a light, Hannah?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Bloody hell, you can still see the factory burning from all the way out here!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: This is no laughing matter, Indra!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Of course it is! We messed up some wicked duke's scheme!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: We... did something really big here.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: At least we can say we've done nothing wrong, yeah?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Let the coppers handle the rest of it.
They say Londinium's so big it defies borders, but at times I feel it's rather small. Wouldn't you agree?

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Who would have thought I would meet you here, Alexandrina. Your Royal Highness.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Who are you?!

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: I'm Morrill, a humble guest at the Cavendish estate. Nobody in particular. And yet, I would say I'm one lucky chap.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You know about the factory... You know what Duke Cavendish is up to.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Though I can boast of sharing some of the Duke's burdens, I was not wholly in the know about His Grace's plans for Londinium.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: However, at this moment, my only concern is you, Your Royal Highness Alexandrina.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: I must say, seeing Your Highness standing before me really does call to mind the sight of His Majesty, all those years ago.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: You and he are so very alike. The same childish sense of justice, the same... price you must pay for clinging to it.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What do you want?

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Your little adventure with your friends this evening... Hardly matters, I say. A few boxes of lost merchandise is hardly anything compared to meeting you.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Come now. At the very least, I'll let your chums leave alive. How about that?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Why should I believe a word you're saying?

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Excuse my impertinence, Your Highness, but the truth is you have no other choice.

steps.name: Earl Morrill
steps.text: Or should I say, you are free to try and escape, but I will be keeping a close eye on your whereabouts.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina! The hell're you doing?!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Stop swinging already! You've nearly beaten him dead!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: *huff*... *huff*...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: It's fine, he's still breathing.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina... What's this all about?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You lot... Get out of here.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The factory, all this, it was all my doing. Nothing to do with anyone else.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Are you havin' a laugh?!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina... What was he saying? Why'd he keep calling you 'Your Royal Highness'?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: ...Because she's the heir to the throne of Victoria.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The daughter of the late King Alistair II, Alexandrina Vina Victoria.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I... I didn't mean to hide it. I just thought... It didn't really matter...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You daft, mate?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I'm not asking who you are, I'm asking why you'd try and shoulder all this by yourself!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Hannah...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Sounds like there's a long story you need to be telling us.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: No time for that! Save it, we need to leave right now!

spans.text: No time for that! Save it, we need to leave
right now

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Where can we go, though?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Out the city.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Right now. This instant. Immediately.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I can't—

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: We're nearly out of time. Once the police notice the factory's up in flames, they'll contact the Defense Forces and shutter each and every port. When that happens, we wouldn't be able to fly out, even if we sprouted wings.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Don't worry about Norport. I'll hold the fort.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Wait, Baird, you're not coming with?! Hey, Morgan, say something, won't you?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I get where she's coming from. The Glasgow Gang's always going to be home to us, Hannah.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Someone's gotta welcome you lot home when you get back, right?

spans.text: Someone's
gotta welcome you lot home when you get back, right?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: People are watching you. But I'm sorry, Vina. We can't protect you. Against real titans like them, the Gang's nothing more than puny little musbeasts.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You were never a Norporter, Vina. Or should I say, never only a Norporter. I knew from the day you joined us.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It's all my fault. I just wanted to protect you all, but... but now, I've dumped a heap of trouble on your laps.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Not wrong. If you're going to blame yourself, though, there's something I hope you keep in mind.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Remember that you owe Norport. Remember that one day, you'll need to come back here to repay everyone.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I swear. I swear I'll come back.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Yeah! It's our turf, after all! We'll snatch it right back someday!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But are you really set on coming with me? There's no need to tangle yourselves in all this.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I'm your trusted advisor, Vina. I'm worried for you.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: If anyone comes looking to bother you, you're gonna need me to help bash their faces in!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Wherever you go, Vina, I will follow.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Never forget, Vina. No matter where you go, the Glasgow Gang will be with you.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I'll keep this place safe. We won it together, after all.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I promise you, Baird. I'll bring everyone back.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Hopefully sooner rather than later.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Here's to us. To the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: To the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Flustered Clerk
steps.text: Dammit, dammit all... M-My Lady! It's the Duke of Cavendish's man!

steps.name: Flustered Clerk
steps.text: My Lady, I-I'll contact Headquarters right away! Even if we must turn all of Londinium upside-down—
Suppress this event.

steps.name: Flustered Clerk
steps.text: Very well, I'm contacting the hospital—What? Suppress it?
I will have my men handle this. Nothing to come will have anything to do with the Norport Police.
Do not worry. The chief of the Royal Police will not come calling on you about this or anyone else on scene, for that matter.

spans.text: Do not worry. The chief of the Royal Police will
not
come calling on you about this or anyone else on scene, for that matter.

steps.name: Flustered Clerk
steps.text: R-Really? How can you be so sure...?
While I cannot fix the future's course, sir, I can guide it towards a path of my liking.
This city will soon be welcoming a host of visitors. Do you not have more important things to handle?

steps.name: Flustered Clerk
steps.text: You... Alright... Very well!
This too is part of your destiny, Vina.

a.text: When we found out about Vina's past, I was amazed, sure, but I was more pleasantly surprised, as it were.

spans.text: When we found out about Vina's past, I was amazed, sure, but I was more pleasantly surprised, as it were.

a.text: I could see the entire story in my mind's eye. A lost heir to the throne, a heroic fantasy rising from the streets.

spans.text: I could see the entire story in my mind's eye. A lost heir to the throne, a heroic fantasy rising from the streets.

a.text: Stories usually start with someone leaving, and end with a reunion. But reality begs to differ.

spans.text: Stories usually start with someone leaving, and end with a reunion. But reality begs to differ.

a.text: When we stepped out on the road away from home, none of us expected the way back could be so fraught with hardship.

spans.text: When we stepped out on the road away from home, none of us expected the way back could be so fraught with hardship.

a.text: I'm fond of the words Dagda spoke once we set foot on our home again, after many, many years away:

spans.text: I'm fond of the words Dagda spoke once we set foot on our home again, after many, many years away:

a.text: 'History is like a sailing ship adrift, and every age sees its share of experienced helmsmen who think to change its course...'

spans.text: 'History is like a sailing ship adrift, and every age sees its share of experienced helmsmen who think to change its course...'

a.text: 'But in the end, none will truly ever know where the sunset and the river will take them.'

spans.text: 'But in the end, none will truly ever know where the sunset and the river will take them.'

steps.name: Gang Member
steps.text: Hey, who're you? Here to get some rounds in the ring?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'd like to ask if this is where the Glasgow Gang is based? I'm looking for Siege. If I understand things right, she's your leader?

steps.name: Gang Member
steps.text: This gym's only got one leader now. She's called Baird.

steps.name: Gang Member
steps.text: Wait a sec... Lookin' at your clothes, you a noble?

steps.name: Gang Member
steps.text: Get out. You ain't welcome here.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Pardon me, then.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You're looking for Vina? You know her?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm... an old friend of hers.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Vina's out on a trip. If you've got something to say, I can pass it on for you.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No, nothing in particular. It's just that as her friend, I'm concerned about her current situation.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Please let her know I'm wishing her all the best, when you can.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Sure. She's doing fine. I'll tell her on your behalf.
Allerdale turns and leaves the messy gym. She knows the woman there wasn't lying. Because she saw the photo hanging on the wall, and the smiling face upon it.
It's not time yet.
In her fit of absent-mindedness, that deep, resonant voice arises in her head once more.
'Allerdale Cumberland.'
'You will meet Vina again, someday.'
